root_cause_analysis.symptom: T1 (`git commit -m "random fix"` from /tmp) returned exit 0 instead of expected exit 2; T3 (`git push origin main` from /tmp) returned exit 0 instead of expected exit 2.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: pretool-git-privilege-guard.py line 221-222 calls `_is_overnight_active()` and exits 0 when no live `.claude/overnight-state-*.json` is found in CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR or os.getcwd(). This narrows the hook to overnight-only sessions, contradicting the spec which explicitly requires the hook to fire in non-overnight (regular Claude Code) sessions.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit: Cycle 2 G4 dev (no SHA — uncommitted) introduced _is_overnight_active() helper and gate-call as a defensive narrowing.
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: G4 dev's docstring (lines 4-19, 40-44) cites 'Interactive sessions where the human is online and supervising every tool call do not need this guard - the human can reject any unwanted git mutation directly.' This is a defensible design argument BUT contradicts spec 5.2.4 line 315 which is the authoritative source of truth.
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: The b5d447e regression (the central failure spec 5.2.4 R4.3 was designed to prevent) occurred in a regular Claude Code session at 2026-04-21 17:45 UTC with CWD=/root, gitBranch=master, prompt '全部commit push'. There was NO live overnight-state file at that time. The current overnight-only hook would have fail-open and the same b5d447e replay would succeed today.
